properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to Penneco Oil Co Inc in Bell Twp, Westmoreland County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-07-25 to Penneco Oil Co Inc in Bell Twp, Westmoreland county. 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Penneco Oil Co Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-07-25
Violation Code: 78.53 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL - Operator failed to design, implement and maintain best management practices and an erosion and sediment control plan in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 102, during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities, including the activities related to siting, drilling, completing, producing, servicing and plugging, constructing, utilizing and restoring the site and access road.
Violation ID: 857644
Permit API: 129-27761
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Bell Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-07-25
Comments: On-site meeting held between Penneco and the Department to review and discuss current site conditions. There is a rock-lined ditch along the SSW edge of the well site (Photos #1, #2) with what appears to be a sump-like structure at the outlet (Photo #3) which appears to be directing water downslope and off of the well site. This ditch does not appear to be properly implemented and/or functioning. Two options were discussed for controlling this stormwater runoff: 1) Installing a culvert that directs water from this existing ditch to the ditch alongside the access road (Photo #4) 2) Installing a ditch on the eastern edge of the well site that directs the water from this existing ditch around the eastern edge of the well site into the ditch alongside the access road (Photo #5) According to the operator, this ditch was installed when the well site was originally built approximately 10 years ago. It was originally vegetated, but was recently widened, deepened, and rocked in response to concerns identified under inspection record 2880181. Based on previous and current inspections, violations are being issued for failure to properly implement and maintain BMPs. The operator agreed to provide a proposed plan to address the stormwater issues to the Department. The Department collected soil conductivity readings utilizing a soil conductivity probe. In the ditch and downslope of this ditch, the readings were 0.20 ms/cm. Upslope, the background readings were 0.04 ms/cm. The Department inquired as to whether a release had ever occurred at this site. The operator stated no, but the brine tank was repaired approximately 5 years ago. The Department inquired as to what prompted this repair. The operator said the brine tank was developing cracks that may have led to a release so the repair was performed as a preventative maintenance. Additional violations may be forthcoming upon further review and investigation. An NOV response is not being requested as options to achieve compliance were discussed with the operator during this inspection.

Comments: Brian Shank and I met Ray Hepler at Farrington and Hepler Gas and Oil, Inc.'s Wheeler W12 well site (API 065-26269) in Washington Twp., Jefferson Co. Ray was onsite remediating the production fluid release first noted on Inspection Record No. 3765883. Soil conductivity readings near the production tank were greater than 1000 pS/cm. Ray stated he will remove this contaminated soil. Ray showed Brian and I a waste manifest for soil from Jefferson County. He stated this was soil disposed from the Wheeler well sites. We asked him to send the Department a copy of this manifest. The pipe stored onsite was loaded onto a trailer for removal. The outstanding violation associated with storing drilling supplies and equipment not needed for production on the well site without written consent of the surface landowner will be closed.After Ray completes the clean up of API 065-26269, please send the Department a report documenting the cause of the spill, the estimated amount of the spill, and the details of the clean up. Please include the soil conductivity reading collected throughout the remediation. Send the Department all waste manifests documenting proper disposal of contaminated soil from API 065-26269. After the Department receives, reviews and accepts the clean up report, the outstanding violations for API 065-26269 will be closed.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/23/2023 to REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC in Hamilton Twp, Tioga county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/23/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 986171
Permit API: 117-22124
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/23/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection at Repsol's Johnson K 02-135 well site located in Hamilton Township, Tioga County on 2/23/2023 at 0935 hours. The weather was 37 degrees with fog. A layer of snow covered the majority of the site today. An Act 9 sign is located at the site entrance.This inspection was conducted in response to a reported release called in to the DEP by Repsol on 2/16/2023. On 2/16/2023 at 0900 hours, a release of 18.7 gallons of produced water mixed with sand was released to the pad surface and containment from a sand trap. Repsol promptly called in the release to the DEP reporting hotline and began cleanup activities. A Repsol representative provided photos of the cleanup to me via email on 2/22/2023.During today's inspection, the impacted area was observed to have been excavated. All impacted material recovered was placed into containers for later disposal. No evidence of any portion of the release remaining was observed today. Pooled water in and around the impacted area was field measured for electrical conductivity ranging from 160 to 320us/cm. Complaint Tracking System (CTS) ID #370057 is tied to this release within CTS.Based on the reported release of 18.7 gallons of produced water to the pad surface and containment, violations of 35 P.S. 691.402(b), 25 Pa. Code 78a.56(a), and 35 P.S. 6018.301 are cited against API #117-22124. However, due to Repsol's timely remediation of the reported release, these violations are considered immediately corrected at this time. Violations from a previous issue cited on 8/10/2022 and 9/2/2022 remain outstanding against API #117-22124. I departed the site at 1100 hours.

Comments: On April 25, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3965337, where violations were issued in response to an estimated 50 barrel release of a brine/crude oil mixture. No impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth were observed during the time of IR 3965337.The Department spoke via phone with Penneco representative Marc Jacobs prior to this inspection, who stated that forecasted storms have delayed start of remediation to Monday, 4/28/2025. In response, the impacted area was covered, and oil absorbent booms and E and S controls were installed downslope.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photos 2 and 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). A gas odor was detected onsite during this inspection. The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 5 and 6). The path of brown staining that was observed traveling downslope from the brine tank has been covered with plastic sheeting in preparation for the forecasted rains. Additional oil absorbent booms have also been placed down slope of the covered impacted area (see photos 8-15). No evidence of visual impacts and/or elevated conductivity were detected down slope of impacted area (see photos 16 and 17).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that the impacted area has been adequately,protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater.Violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: Follow-up site inspection on August 31, 2020 at ARD's COP Tract 231 well pad. Prior to my site inspection I spoke with Rick Hall of ARD via phone. The contractor discovered during excavation a small hole in the buried 2" steel line, which was the result of the undetermined amount of fluids released on August 28, 2020. According to Mr. Hall, approximately 50 tons of impacted gravel/soil were removed during excavation on August 28, 2020. Impacted gravel/soils were placed on secondary containment stationed onsite and the materials were covered. Impacted gravel/soils were observed during my inspection. Water was observed on the secondary containment with field screenings ranging from 52.8 uS/cm- 65.1 uS/cm. The Department recommends removing the rain water from the secondary containment.After excavation and repairing a section of the 2" dump line, the operator opted to leave the trench open and staked off with orange safety fence. According to Mr. Hall, there are three pipe lines running in the same ditch line. The first is the 2" steel dump line located at approximately 2' 8" deep below the surface. A 3" steel discharge line located in the same ditch line and a 6" steel suction line located approximately 4 feet away from the 2" dump line and is approximately 5' 8" below the surface. Mr. Hall stated that a bed of sand is located beneath the 6" suction line and conductivity readings were elevated in sections of that sand. Tuscarora Geological & Environmental Services collected samples from the impacted sand area. Mr. Hall requested that the sample results be expedited. Samples results are pending.While I was onsite I viewed the open trench. I screened throughout the 2" dump line side of the trench and readings ranged from 0.100 mS/cm to 0.300 mS/cm. I screened on the 6" suction line side of the trench and I was getting elevated readings >4.00 mS/cm in an approximate 2' diameter area. These elevated readings were adjacent to where the 2" dump line was repaired. As I moved away from that 2' diameter area, screenings dropped to 0.100 mS/cm to 0.400 mS/cm.No new violations have been cited. Outstanding violations remain.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a64a(b) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – All regulated substances, including solid wastes and other regulated substances in equipment or vehicles, failed to be managed within secondary containment on the well site.
Violation ID: 8245071
Permit API: 125-29170
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Cecil Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/12/2025
Comments: On August 12, 2025, the Department conducted an Incident Inspection of Range Resources Conner Samuel well site, located in Cecil Township, Washington County in response to a spill that was reported to the DEP hotline on 8/11/2025 at 8:44pm by Range. Accompanying on today's inspection is Range Resources representative Kevin Rudd.According to the report and Mr. Rudd, after finishing the cement job on the 4H, a flow line became over pressurized due to a valve being left closed. This resulted in a 10 cap dislodging from the flow line and releasing approximately 21 gallons of a synthetic oil based mud (SOBM) fine mist on to the graveled well pad and approximately 42 gallons on to the secondary containment. According to Range, prior to this inspection, the fine mist release was remediated in accordance with 78a66(c)(1) and disposal documents will be provided to the Department upon its receipt.At the time of this inspection, the Act 9 Sign was observed at the access road entrance with all required information posted on it, and in the on-site mailbox was the Emergency Response Plan and Preparedness, Prevention and Contingency Plan, both of which had all required components. The access road was observed to be stabilized with gravel and the well site perimeters were observed to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the release area to be approximately 12ft x 20ft and comprised of had freshly laid gravel. No SOBM was observed on the gravel or on the secondary containment in this area at the time of this inspection. The Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the gravel well pad in this release area, and collected soil conductivity readings of 0.0002 mS, in three different locations as well as 0.0651 mS, and 0.0028 mS. These soil conductivity readings are comparable to the background soil conductivity reading of 0.0213 mS, which was collected upslope and adjacent to the well site in a vegetated area.At the time of this inspection, the Department requested Safety Data Sheets (SDSs) for the SOBM involved in the release as well as secondary containment inspection logs. At the time of this inspection, Mr. Rudd provided the Department with the secondary containment logs and attempted to email the Department an electronic copy of the SDSs, however, that email was not received, therefore the Department is again requesting that SDSs for the SOBM be provided to the Department within 2 business days of the receipt of this inspection report.Based on observations made at the time of this inspection, it appears that Range remediated the release in accordance with 78a66(c)(1), therefore, violations are noted and immediately corrected.Transmittal of this inspection report is delayed due to an app IT error.

The CAPPUCCI 2H, N2H, 4H, N4H, 102H and HJMM WYO 1H wells. These tests are being performed in response to a new gas migration investigation in area underway by The Department. Gas detections were then confirmed by The Department, using a MSA ALTAIR 5X gas meter, last calibrated on 5/20/2020. Gas: 83 % (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened back to vent to production tanks @ 11:00. ** The presence of pressure and gas was detected in the (13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad with the exception of the Cappucci Wyo 2H which is a (2) string well. This is indicative of defective cement which is a violation of Title 25-chapter 78a.86 - Defective casing or cementing. The Department requests, in writing by 7/01/20, how CALLC plans to comply with Ch. 78a.86.

Report Details
Inspection Client: TURM OIL INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/02/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 957712
Permit API: 063-34032
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Cherryhill Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/02/2022
Comments: On 6/2/22 at 0900 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Turm Oil, Inc.'s Paul Strong 4 well (API 063-34032) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. Mr. Bill Davis with Turm Oil was also present during the inspection. The inspection was conducted in response to a complaint, received by the Department on 6/1/22, of oil and produced water being released from a production fluids tank that was being removed from the site.I spoke with the complainant, the operator, and Mr. Davis on 6/1/22. The operator informed me that the well was sold to Rosebud Mining back in March; however there is no record of a well transfer filed with the Department. During our phone call, Mr. Davis informed me that the tank removal and release occurred around 1100 hrs. on 5/31/22. He estimated that approximately 10 gallons of crude oil and production fluid was released when removing the tank, and stated that some absorbent material was placed near the well and was subsequently containerized. Mr. Davis also acknowledged that some released fluid was covered up during regrading of the site.Upon inspection of the site, oil stained soil and vegetation was observed, beginning at the regraded area of the well pad, and continuing along a drainage ditch adjacent to the pad. There was a strong crude oil odor present. The impacted water in the ditch flowed to a nearby ephemeral stream where a slight sheen was observed. The black plastic bag containing the absorbent material Mr. Davis previously applied was located at the base of the well head; however, no additional measures were taken to prevent the material from reaching Waters of the Commonwealth. I advised Mr. Davis to place absorbent boom or pads to prevent further downstream impacts. I also advised Mr. Davis that regulations require removal of the pollutant from the soil and water within 15 days. In addition, I requested that Mr. Davis reinstall a well tag with the permit number on the well head.The release was not reported to the Department. Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.66(b), and78.66(e) are cited and will be immediately closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), CSL 402(b), 78.54, 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(a), and SWMA 610(1) are being cited for the release of crude oil and production fluid onto the ground and into Waters of the Commonwealth. These violations will be resolved upon remediation and temporary stabilization of the site, and submission of waste manifests for the disposal of impacted material to the Department.

Unconventional Y

Comments The Department (Jon Sassi-DEP, EPS) received a phone call from Mike Demming (Senior Regulator Analyst-SWN) on 2/7/17 at 1601 hours to self report a release of less than 5 gallons of diesel fuel. The release was discovered at 1405 hours. Mr. Demming explained that a US Well Services heater trailer (line heater which keeps water from freezing during hydraulic fracturing operations and has since been taken to their yard for repair) was exiting the location and was tilting forward on the access road when the diesel fuel overflowed the belly pan and was released to the access road. The diesel fuel traveled along the access road being carried by stormwater (raining at the time of the release) downslope and flowing into the roadside ditch along Hawk Road. The belly pan is used to collect leaks and overflow from the heater trailer. The operator failed to clean the belly pan prior to demobilization. A mini excavator will be used to remove any impacted material and a vac truck will remove and impacted fluid. SWN will conduct PID screening after excavation. He stated that the visibly impacted material will be taken to the Tunnel landfill via the Meshoppen Rail-yard. The Department (Jon Sassi and I) arrived on site to conduct an Incident Inspection in response to Mr. Demming's report. At the time of the inspection Consolidated Well Services was drilling out frac plugs. We met with Justin Johnson (Construction Supervisor-John Miller) at the time of the inspection. Mike Demming later arrived on site and both gentlemen joined us during our inspection. We walked along the access road and moved stone around in areas that appeared to have residual sheen. We followed the residual sheen upslope to an area on the access road that appeared to be the point of impact. Mr. Demming field screened the areas and got readings between 0.7-112 PPM on his PID. Ed Blystone (Well Site Supervisor) met with us during the screening. We then walked down the access road where Mr. Demming explained that an approximate 1 quart of diesel fuel was recovered by the vac truck at the Hawk Road roadside ditch. They also removed stone and some material beneath the stone. When we inspected the area, the ditch was already reworked and new stone was in place. Failure to maintain E&S BMP's

Failure to maintain E&S BMP's
ID: 778519 Date: 2017-02-15 00:00:00 Type: Environmental Health & Safety
91.34(A) - ACTIVITIES UTILIZING POLLUTANTS - Failure to take necessary measures to prevent the substances from directly or indirectly reaching waters of this Commonwealth, through accident, carelessness, maliciousness, hazards of weather or from another cause. During this inspection, it was found that sheen was still present. A SWN representative identified, prior to our inspection, that residual product was existing on site and deployed sorbent pads and booms. While on site, I requested that they remove any additional impacted material and re-screen those areas.
ID: 778518 Date: 2017-02-15 00:00:00 Type: Environmental Health & Safety
CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department. Diesel fuel was released to the ground causing a potential for pollution to enter the waters of the commonwealth.
ID: 778521 Date: 2017-02-15 00:00:00 Type: Environmental Health & Safety
78.56(a) - PITS AND TANKS FOR TEMPORARY CONTAINMENT - Operator failed to contain pollutional substances and wastes from the drilling, altering, completing, recompleting, servicing and plugging the well, including brines, drill cuttings, drilling muds, oils, stimulation fluids, well treatment and servicing fluids, plugging and drilling fluids other than gases in a pit, tank or series of pits and tanks. The operator failed to check and clean the belly pan of the heater trailer prior to demobilizing, causing the release.

No spills, leaks, or releases are observed at this time.- Well appears to be buried at this time (Photo 18).- CFS on-site appears to be installed and functioning properly. No E and S issues observed on site at this time.The Department recommends the operator stabilize the two points of accelerated erosion and sedimentation and install CFS per the E and S Plan. Violations remain outstanding for accelerated erosion and sedimentation along the access road and for failing to construct the site in accordance with the E and S Plan.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/09/2021 to SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC in Middlebury Twp, Tioga county. 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES - Reporting releases - Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: SENECA RESOURCES CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/09/2021
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1 - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report spills and releases of regulated substances to the Department.
Violation ID: 910054
Permit API: 117-20562
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga
Municipality: Middlebury Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/09/2021
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a ROUTINE inspection of the Seneca Resources - Gee 832 Well Site located in Middlebury Twp, Tioga Co. on 3/9/21 @0950 hours. The weather was 45 degrees and sunny. No activity or personnel was observed onsite. The site consists of a long access road, well pad and perimeter controls. The majority of the well pad was clear of snow and ice with some piles still melting along the edges. Frozen fluid was observed in the infiltration basin off the corner of the well pad. What appeared to be frost was observed on the production tank onsite. Upon closer inspection, the tank appeared to be covered in crystalized salt originating from the top hatch of the tank . The front 1/3 of the "Highland" production tank and a small ~5'x5' area in front of the tank were observed to have the salt material on it. The pad surface in front of the tank was observed damp. Soil conductivity of the damp area was measured with a Groline soil conductivity probe and found to be >4.0mS/cm directly adjacent to the yellow barrel. Other areas screened within the 5'x5' area in front of the tank were found to have a field measured conductivity of 2.18mS/cm and 1.7mS/cm. Due to the lack of cell phone service onsite, I traveled to a nearby well pad with known cell phone service to contact the operator. I then returned to the well site to complete the inspection. Seneca representative Jake Chambers arrived onsite in response to the release. Mr. Chambers and I discussed the possible causes for the release and the impacted area. Mr. Chambers stated he would immediately mobilize people and equipment to wash down the tank and remove any impacted pad material Jeff Passerrello, Seneca Resources, submitted confirmation of the remediation of the release at the Gee 832 Well Pad via email. Mr. Passerrello stated the release was estimated to have happened between Sunday 3/7/21 and the morning of the DEP inspection. The operator had unloaded the wells to the production tanks on Sunday, which they believe caused a mist of production fluid to coat the tank and gravel. The release was estimated to be approximately 5 gallons. Crews removed the impacted gravel, which was placed into 3 drums. A depth of 3" of material was removed from in front of the tank. The tank was also cleaned with freshwater and scrub brushes. Violations of the following regulations are cited as Immediately Corrected: 25 Pa Code 78a57(a)Control, Storage and disposal of production fluids CSL402(b)Potential Pollution SWMA 301 Management of residual waste I departed the site at 1145 hours.

Comments: One November 13 2025, the Department conducted a complaint inspection in regards to a complaint submitted to the Department on 11/12/2025. There appeared to be an area along the access road with deep ruts beginning to form (photo 2). The Department recommends the operator ensure the access road is maintained. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection.At the time of inspection, the well appeared equipped for production. A well tag and well posting was present at the time of thisinspection. There were no observed on going leaks or discharge of fluid on the ground or around the wellhead.Upon inspection of the production equipment, the Department observed severely corroded production lines running to/from the production tank. The corrosion has lead to large holes forming in the lines (photos 9-11). The Department did not observe any signs of a release from these corroded production lines. Soil conductivity readings were taken in the soil beneath the holes in the lines with readings of 0.27mS, and 0.17mS. These readings appeared comparable to the background conductivity reading of 0.19mS.The production tank appeared to be sound with no visible leaks, however appeared to be empty. The Department recommends the operator remove the production tank if it is no longer necessary for production.Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the corroded production lines.

Comments: On 8/31/2026, the Department conducted a surface inspection of the Orr 14 OG well in Washington Township, Fayette County. This inspection follows-up to IR 4266621, where violations were issued for failure implement adequate Erosion and Sedimentation control measures prior to conducting earth disturbances on the access road, which is resulting in a threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth. Diversified representative Jared Walker was present on site during this inspection.At the time of inspection, the following was observed:- The access road appears to be a multi-use road that is shared with additional Diversified well sites. Some tire rutting was observed in the shared access road. No Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) is installed at the access road entrance. Step 1.3 of the E and S/Restoration plan construction sequence is to install a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) at the access road entrance prior to conducting earth disturbances.- The well site is located within a forested agricultural area. Compost Filter Sock (CFS) is installed downslope of the well site. Portions of the compost filter sock are holding minor amounts of sediment. In other portions of the CFS, the stakes appear to be dislodged. This does not appear to be affecting the functionality of the CFS at the time of inspection. However, the Department recommends that the Operator conduct maintenance on the CFS. Violations may be forthcoming pending re-evaluation of this location in a future inspection. Rig mats are being installed on the saturated ground around the gas well. The E and S/Restoration plan and a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) are located at the Navaho Hollow Road entrance, which will not be used for well plugging operations. The E and S/Restoration plan is not specific to the Connellsville Street access road, which is being used for plugging operations. - The gas well is equipped with a well tag. A plugging rig and well plugging equipment have been staged on site. The Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) was installed on site during this inspection by Mr. Walker (Photo 24).- Upon exiting the site toward Connellsville Street, the Department observed loose soil remaining adjacent to an apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run (Photo 2). Although no sediment was observed entering this apparent unnamed tributary to Downers Run at the time of inspection, it is actively under threat by this site since no E and S control measures are installed in this location. Mr. Walker stated during this inspection that an E and S/Restoration plan specific to the Connellsville Street access road is drafted, but needs to be printed and installed on site. Mr. Walker also stated that correction of the ongoing threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOTC), and installation of a Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) and additional CFS will be conducted on the day following this inspection.The Department continues to recommend that the operator take immediate action to cease ongoing threats to the Waters of the Commonwealth.Based on today's inspection, the violations for failure implement adequate Erosion and Sedimentation control measures will remain outstanding, as the threat to the Waters of the Commonwealth remains and tire rutting is occurring on site. Additional violations are being issued for failure to follow the E and S/Restoration plan and for failure to have an updated copy of the E and S/Restoration plan available on site.The violation issued in IR 4265922 for failure to post the Operator's information required by OGA 3211(G) on site will be closed in IR 4269231.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 12/19/2022 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/19/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 979235
Permit API: 081-21881
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 12/19/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator about a release of an estimated 42 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and freshwater to the surface of pad B. The frac is on-going on Pad B. The site was snow-covered during this inspection. I met with EQT representative Zachary Subra upon arriving on Pad B. He showed me the location of the fluid discovered earlier in the day. The modular aboveground storage structure (MASS) present on the pad is in the northeast corner of the pad. The fluid on the pad surface is northeast of the MASS. The fluid in this area had an electrical conductivity (EC) of greater than 19.99 mS/cm. A thin layer of fluid covered approximately 20 square feet of the visible pad surface. The secondary containments for the heaters and pumps near this area of the pad had only snow and ice within them. The secondary containment at the southeast side of the MASS had fluid in it with EC of 700 to 1100 mS/cm. This containment appears to be in good condition and did not appear to be at risk of over-topping. Mr. Subra stated that there is also fluid with elevated EC at the northeast outlet of the north stormwater channel. The fluid was observed beginning at the east end of the rip rap at the end of the channel and extended for approximately 10-15ft farther to the northeast. This flow did not appear to reach the line of compost filter sock present approximately 5ft farther to the northeast. The fluid here ranged from 11.85 mS/cm to >19.99 mS/cm. The pad side slopes and the full length of the north stormwater channel was snow covered. The ground at the toe of the east pad side slope was also snow-covered and appeared frozen. Mr. Subra stated during the inspection that the suspected source of the fluid is the MASS since no other source could be identified. He stated that the space between the primary and secondary walls on the MASS contains fluid but the sensors on the MASS had not alerted them to elevated EC in this space. He also stated toward the end of this inspection that these sensors had been recalibrated and that they were now indicating that the fluid in this space has a high EC reading but he did not state what the reading was. I made the following recommendations to Mr. Subra during this inspection. The Department recommends not adding any additional fluid to the MASS. The Department recommends installing a sump at the east end of the north stormwater channel and collecting the fluid from this sump for the duration of the frac. The Department recommends emptying and disassembling the MASS. The Department recommends installing a trench, if possible, at the northeast corner of the pad to collect fluid before it makes its way into the north stormwater channel. The Department recommends monitoring this trench and the sump for electrical conductivity. I took sample 0718-197 from the east end of the north stormwater channel. I took sample 0718-198 from the northeast corner of the pad, next to the northeast side of the MASS. Both samples will be sent to the state laboratory. Sample 0718-197 will be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Al, Br, and Li. Sample 0718-198 will be analyzed for the 942 metals plus Al, Br, and Li. On 12/20/22 Rick Hall of EQT emailed the Department a report detailing the results of EQT's investigation of the release. The report states, in summary, that a combination of things led to the release including a hole in the secondary containment liner of the interstitial space between each wall of the MASS, an incorrectly installed electrical conductivity meter in this space which lead to inconsistent readings, and a check valve installed backwards which led to a truck driver successfully off-loading produced fluid into the interstitial space. The report also stated that EQT is committed to pursuing remediation of this release under Act 2.Violations noted.

properties.content:

Permit API: 081-21881
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/19/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted after multiple releases occurred on Pad B. The wells on Pad B are in flowback. Secondary containment is installed surrounding the well heads. According to Zac Subra with EQT, earlier in the day less than 5 gallons of fluid was sprayed on the pad surface and onto the secondary containment around the well heads from a valve attached to a sand separator next to one of the well heads. The area of the pad surface had already been scraped by Tobias Machinery during this inspection. Some sand from the produced fluid spray was observed on the secondary containment.The sump remains installed at the northeast end of the north stormwater channel. The electrical conductivity (EC) of the fluid in the sump was 2.60 mS/cm. Multiple seeps were observed coming from the well pad side slope and the topsoil stockpile which were flowing into the sump. The EC of this fluid was 3.55 mS/cm. The fluid coming from the seeps had a red/orange rust color to it. Mr. Subra said that EQT believes that the color is likely due to iron content in the soil. The fluid in the north central portion of the north stormwater channel had an EC between 3.55 to 3.76 mS/cm.Mr. Subra said that final samples have been taken for the Act 2 remediation report but that the sample results were not yet available as of the time of this inspection. Multiple evaporators are also in operation on Pad B. The secondary containment for the evaporators appears to be in good condition. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs appear to be in good condition.On Pad A, six wells are still in production. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition. The access road and adjacent pipeline right-of-way appeared to be dry. No new sediment discharges were observed. Some of the stormwater culverts under the access road were partially filled with sediment. Mr. Subra said that Tobias would be cleaning out the culverts later that day.Violations remain outstanding for the reported produced fluid release from the MASS on Pad B from 12/19/22 against permit 081-21881.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21879 for the reported release of produced fluid from clam shell boxes in the northwest area of Pad B, in the area of the dancefloor, from 2/6/23.Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21880 for the reported discovery of additional fluid with elevated electrical conductivity in the northcentral area of the pad in the area of the Sand X boxes.

properties.content:
Report Details

Permit API: 015-23722
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Leroy Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2/03/2023
Comments: Incident Inspection of Chesapeake's "SGL12 M North B" Marcellus well site.Chesapeake hydraulically fractured the 4 Marcellus wells here in November 2022.Danielle Schaad called the DEP yesterday to report an estimated 1 barrel release of production liquid to the pad surface.I spoke with Danielle Schaad and Chris Lee (both Chesapeake) on site. Lee discovered production liquid in the yellow takeout can, and moist soil around the production tank yesterday. They explained that two days ago a vac truck caused the release of production liquid while transferring it from the tank, but did not report it to Chesapeake. MR Dirt is excavating the moist pad material around the production tank. Creston Environmental and I screened the moist soil around the tank for electrical conductivity (EC) with Hanna Groline Soil Test probes. Both probes maxed out (>4.00 mS/cm). Pad material not impacted by the spill is frozen solid, and we could not get EC readings from it. Chesapeake plans to remove the production tank on Monday February 23 to excavate any impacted pad material under it. The production liquid will flow into 4 GasBuster tanks in the mean time.Violations for the spill are cited to the 015-23722 permit.Cannot assess soil stabilization today because of ~2" of snow coverage. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed. I did not see any pooled water on site, just snow/ice.Air temp 8FJLP

Complaints Tracking System (CTS) ID #394552 is tied to the release in CTS.On 1/12/2026, Blackhill Energy reported to the DEP that approximately 1 barrel (42 gallons) of produced fluid was discovered to have been released to the pad surface at ~0730 hours. Blackhill reported the release within 2 hours of discovery and began remediation as soon as possible. Throughout the remediation process, temperatures rose, thawing some of the pad material and requiring a couple locations of deeper excavation. Impacted materials were placed within 2 lined residual waste containers onsite (photo #5). During my inspection, pad materials within the impacted areas were field measured for electrical conductivity and returned readings ranging from 0.1 to 2.2mS/cm. Fluids located closest to the impacted area were field measured for electrical conductivity below 1.0mS/cm. The DEP recommends continuing screening and recovery of any impacted materials and collecting characterization samples to confirm that cleanup is complete. Based on the reported release of ~1 barrel of produced fluids to the pad surface, outside of secondary containment, violations of the following are cited against API #015-22301 at this time:25 Pa. A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA (#372946), Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216.The following was observed during the inspection:The access road and well site appear to be stable, with no evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation observed during this inspection (photos 1-6). No significant ruts were observed upon entry, and the Department was able to access the well site by vehicle. No Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls and/or evidence of earth disturbances related to plugging operations were observed at the time of inspection.The actual gas well location closely matches the coordinates obtained via Department records. No plugging equipment was observed on site during this inspection. Production reports obtained via Department database show that no gas was produced by this well in 2024 and in 2025. The API number is posted on the well tag (photos 9 and 10). The operator's information is posted on the meter box (photo 8). However, portions of the operator's information are no longer legible due to peeling and deterioration of the posting. Although no brine tank was observed on site, review of historic satellite imagery found that a brine tank was formerly installed on site (photo 11). Soil conductivity readings were taken in a rocky area lacking vegetation at the former brine tank location (66.2-221 /), which appeared to be comparable with the surrounding soil (139.6 /). (photos 13-15)Based on observations from this inspection a violation shall be issued against the peeling and deteriorated operator's information posting.

Permit API: 051-23971
Unconventional: No

Comments: On 6/15/2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of the Wilson 5 well site in Springhill Township, Fayette County. This inspection was conducted in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug the well, which was received by the Department from the operator on 6/11/2026. A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA (#372946), Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216.The following was observed during the inspection:The access road and well site appear to be stable, with no evidence of accelerated erosion and sedimentation observed during this inspection (photos 1-6). No significant ruts were observed upon entry, and the Department was able to access the well site by vehicle. No Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) controls and/or evidence of earth disturbances related to plugging operations were observed at the time of inspection.The actual gas well location closely matches the coordinates obtained via Department records. (photos 13-15)Based on observations from this inspection a violation shall be issued against the peeling and deteriorated operator's information posting.
